security_feature_bypassed: Access control on the subsystem debug-intent flag. SS_DEBUG_INTENT.debug_intent is the gate that decides whether the debug-unlock request and unlock-level registers are writable at all, and its definition permits a write only over the uncore DMI port while the part is unlocked or in manufacturing lifecycle. The audited write qualifier is the logical inverse of that policy, so the flag is armed when no DMI write is issued and on a debug-locked production part, while the one write the policy does permit is discarded.
finding:
src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:828-830 builds the write qualifier for SS_DEBUG_INTENT.debug_intent as strap_we_pre_fuse_done | ~(|{cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en, (cptra_uncore_dmi_reg_addr != DMI_REG_SS_DEBUG_INTENT)}). Transcribing that expression into an exhaustive truth table over its two inputs shows it equals (~wr_en & addr==DMI_REG_SS_DEBUG_INTENT): it is the polarity inverse of the write enable and agrees with the intended form on only two of four input rows. Every other strap register served by the same DMI port on the same lines uses the positive form, for example :825-826 which writes strap_we_pre_fuse_done | (cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en & (cptra_uncore_dmi_reg_addr == DMI_REG_SS_STRAP_GENERIC_3)). A census that counts constructs without naming the audited signal measures 17 positive sibling qualifiers against exactly 1 negated reduction, and 76 address equality comparisons against exactly 1 address inequality. Both singletons are the audited line.

The inversion also inverts the access policy, not merely the enable. The lifecycle and lock state reach this expression on one path only: :774-776 qualifies cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_en on (~debug_locked | lifecycle==DEVICE_MANUFACTURING), and :780 folds that into cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en, which is precisely the term being negated. Negating it means the write lands when the part is locked and out of manufacturing lifecycle, and is discarded in the one state the register's own definition allows. src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_subsystem_reg.rdl:142 states the access as TAP Access [in debug/manuf mode]: RW, and :143 defines the field as sw = r; hw = rw, so software is not the intended writer at all and the DMI port is the only write path.

The address is not dead: src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_pkg.sv:96 fixes DMI_REG_SS_DEBUG_INTENT = 7'h63, and the port reaches the block from the JTAG debug module through src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:632-633 and :1528-1529. The file's own comment at :887 asserts that debug intent is latched on the rising edge of cptra_pwrgood and may not be modified until cold reset; the measurement below contradicts that sentence in the same tree. The existing project bench never exercises the path, because src/soc_ifc/tb/soc_ifc_tb.sv:456-460 ties the DMI port off at addr=7'h0 and wr_en=1'h0.

Simulation of one unmodified soc_ifc_top driven only through its ports, with debug_locked=1 and lifecycle=PRODUCTION, confirms both halves. Presenting address 7'h63 with wdata[0]=1 and the write enable low sets debug_intent=1 with no DMI write ever issued; presenting the neighbouring address 7'h62 identically leaves it at 0, so the decode is live; presenting 7'h63 with wdata[0]=0 leaves it at 0, so the stored value is attacker-chosen. In MANUFACTURING lifecycle a legitimate DMI write with reg_en=1, wr_en=1 and wdata[0]=1 leaves debug_intent=0. A pwrgood reset clears the flag, which bounds the defect.
detection_method: Located by CSBC, an LLM-driven analysis method that reasons over a single tree and reports register-transfer sites whose behaviour contradicts sibling lines of the same block, the block's own comments, the access policy in its own register definition, or idioms repeated tree-wide. The candidate here was raised as a write qualifier whose Boolean form is the odd one out among the qualifiers assigned beside it. It was then convicted on its own evidence inside this tree: a scripted structural audit of the submitted sources including an exhaustive truth table over the transcribed expression (26 of 26 gates, result=PASS), a directed simulation of one unmodified soc_ifc_top driven only through its ports (checks=5 fails=2 witness_hits=1, four covers at 1, result=PASS), and a negative control in which restoring the sibling positive form on a scratch copy flips the identical bench (witness_hits=0, both defect covers at 0, tb_fails=0, two code lines added and two removed, both anti-vacuity controls still at 1). No external repository, no other revision of this design, and no expected-answer list was consulted at any point.
security_impact:
debug_intent is the enable for the subsystem debug-unlock surface, so making it attacker-settable moves that whole surface from disabled to available on a production part that is supposed to be locked. src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:897 exports the field as cptra_ss_debug_intent. Inside the same file the flag gates 11 consumers, of which 6 are debug-unlock response fields at :929-934; :924 and :925 make MANUF_DBG_UNLOCK_REQ and PROD_DBG_UNLOCK_REQ software-writable only while it is set, and :946 releases the write lock on SS_SOC_DBG_UNLOCK_LEVEL when it is set. An attacker holding the JTAG lines therefore only has to present an address to convert registers that were hardware-locked into software-writable ones, with no debug authorisation, no unlock ceremony and no write transaction. That is an integrity break on a security policy flag whose own definition in the tree says it cannot be written in this state, and the file comment at :887 says it cannot be written at all after cold reset.

The same inversion has an availability cost in the opposite direction: the legitimate manufacturing-mode write, which is the one the register is defined to accept, is discarded, so a genuine authorised debug-unlock flow cannot set the flag through its intended path. No secret is read out by the defect itself, so this is an access-control and integrity defect rather than a disclosure one. The effect is bounded by cptra_pwrgood: a cold reset returns the flag to 0, which measurement confirms, and the flag alone does not complete an unlock, it only opens the door to requesting one.
proposed_mitigation: Replace the negated reduction at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:829-830 with the positive conjunction every sibling on the same DMI port uses, so the qualifier reads strap_we_pre_fuse_done | (cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en & (cptra_uncore_dmi_reg_addr == DMI_REG_SS_DEBUG_INTENT)), matching :825-826. That two-line change is exactly the negative control performed here, and it flips both violating checks to passing while leaving both anti-vacuity controls and the containment case intact.

Add an assertion that SS_DEBUG_INTENT.debug_intent.we is never asserted while cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en is low and strap_we_pre_fuse_done is low, which fails immediately on the audited form and holds on the corrected one.

Add a lint or review rule over the qualifier assignments at :797-830 requiring every DMI-served register to use the same positive (write enable AND address equality) shape, so a single register cannot silently carry a different Boolean form from its 17 neighbours.

Reconcile the comment at :887 with the implementation once the qualifier is fixed, since as written it claims a write immunity after cold reset that the DMI path does not provide, and that claim is what makes the audited line look intentional.
exploit_or_attack_flow: The part is in its most locked configuration: security_state.debug_locked=1 and device_lifecycle=DEVICE_PRODUCTION. Cold reset has completed and the DMI port is idle, so debug_intent reads 0, measured as case=control_reset_leaves_debug_intent_clear PASS.

An attacker with physical access to the JTAG pins reaches the uncore DMI port. The debug module drives it into the block through src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:632-633, which reaches the soc_ifc_top instance at :1528-1529. No debug authorisation is required to place values on this port, only physical access, and the lock state is supposed to be what stops writes from taking effect.

The attacker presents address 7'h63, DMI_REG_SS_DEBUG_INTENT per src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_pkg.sv:96, with wdata[0]=1 and the DMI write enable deliberately left low. Because :774-776 and :780 fold the lock and lifecycle checks into cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en, and :829-830 negates that whole term, the write qualifier asserts.

src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:891 supplies cptra_uncore_dmi_reg_wdata[0] as the data, so the attacker's chosen bit is captured. Measured as addr=7'h63 wdata[0]=1 wr_en=0 -> debug_intent=1, reported by the bench as BUG_N001_WITNESS_OBSERVED debug_intent set with no DMI write issued, in debug-locked production. Presenting wdata[0]=0 on the same address yields debug_intent=0, confirming the value is attacker-chosen and not a stuck 1.

The neighbouring address 7'h62 driven with the identical attacker action leaves debug_intent=0, so the observation is not a dead address decode asserting the qualifier for every address. Measured as case=control_addr_mismatch_no_write PASS.

With the flag now set, src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:924 and :925 make MANUF_DBG_UNLOCK_REQ and PROD_DBG_UNLOCK_REQ software-writable, :946 drops the write lock on SS_SOC_DBG_UNLOCK_LEVEL, and the six response fields at :929-934 become live, so the debug-unlock request surface is open on a part whose lock state should have refused it.

The mirror image completes the proof that the policy is inverted rather than bypassed. After a cold reset, in DEVICE_MANUFACTURING lifecycle, a legitimate DMI write with reg_en=1, wr_en=1 and wdata[0]=1 is discarded: measured as after a legitimate DMI write -> debug_intent=0. The write succeeds only in the state the register definition at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_subsystem_reg.rdl:142 forbids and fails in the state it permits.

Containment: re-arming the flag through the defect and then asserting a pwrgood cold reset returns debug_intent to 0, measured as case=containment_pwrgood_reset_clears PASS, so the exposure lasts for the current power cycle rather than persisting.
